deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the Paris prize essay (Commentatio mathematica, 1861). Following Weber and Dedekind, the curvature tensor is written here as (ιι',ι''ι''') = -2 R_{ιι'ι''ι'''}. The convention is R_{1212} = K (g11 g22 - g12^2), and g_{ιι'} = b_{ιι'}.

The previous page defines the 'variational' expression
II = δδ Σ b ds ds - 2 dδ Σ b ds δs + dd Σ b δs δs,
with the second variations normalized geodesically (the δ' conditions). It shows that
II = Σ (ιι',ι''ι''') (ds_ι δs_ι' - ds_ι' δs_ι)(ds_ι'' δs_ι''' - ds_ι''' δs_ι'').
My check in Riemann normal coordinates gives II = -2 R(ds,δs,ds,δs). This matches if the sum runs over unordered index pairs ι<ι', ι''<ι''' (or equivalently carries a factor 1/4).

On this page:

(a) Invariance. II is built from the quadratic form Σ b ds ds and the d/δ calculus alone. Hence under any change of independent variables it goes over into the same expression, formed by the same law from the transformed form. In modern terms, R is a tensor.

(b) Flat case. If the b are constant, all p (Christoffel symbols) and all second derivatives vanish, so every coefficient (ιι',ι''ι''') = 0. Therefore a necessary condition for Σ b ds ds to be transformable into a form with constant coefficients is that II vanish identically, i.e. R ≡ 0.

(c) Sectional curvature. Define
(III) K(ds,δs) = -1/2 · II / [ (Σ b ds ds)(Σ b δs δs) - (Σ b ds δs)^2 ].
- K is invariant under change of variables, since numerator and denominator are both invariants.
- K is unchanged under ds → α ds + β δs, δs → γ ds + δ δs. Implicit step (mine): both bivector factors in the numerator, and the Gram determinant in the denominator, scale by (αδ-βγ)^2. So K depends only on the 2-plane spanned by ds and δs.
- With the normalization above, K = R(d,δ,d,δ)/(g(d,d)g(δ,δ) - g(d,δ)^2), i.e. the modern sectional curvature.

(d) Invariants for equivalence. Riemann says the maximum and minimum of K over all planes depend neither on the coordinate form nor on the chosen ds, δs. Hence from these values one can recognize whether two such forms can be transformed into each other.

(e) Geometric interpretation. sqrt(Σ b ds ds) is regarded as the line element of an n-dimensional space transcending intuition. From a point (s_1..s_n), draw all shortest lines (geodesics) whose initial directions are α ds + β δs. The text continues on p.16: these form a surface, developable into ordinary space, whose Gaussian curvature at the point equals (III). This is the geodesic-surface definition of sectional curvature, the same as in the 1854 Habilitationsvortrag.

Purpose. These are tools for the prize question: deciding when the conductivity form Σ b ds ds can be brought to constant coefficients. For n = 3, p.16 gives six equations, of which three are independent.
errors: Claim (d) is overstated as a decision criterion. Agreement of the extreme values of the sectional curvature at corresponding points is necessary but not in general sufficient for local isometry. (For the actual application, flatness, R≡0, is necessary and sufficient, and Riemann asserts sufficiency on p.16 without proof.)

Normalization of the sum in (II)/(III). With (ιι',ι''ι''') = -2R_{ιι'ι''ι'''} and a sum over all ordered index quadruples, -1/2·II/Gram would give 4K. The formula is correct, giving exactly K, only if each unordered pair (ι,ι'), (ι'',ι''') is counted once. The page leaves this implicit.

Not on this page, but affecting (II)/(III): in equation (I) as transcribed on the previous page, the quadratic Christoffel term has the wrong sign. Redoing Riemann's own derivation (∂p/∂s''' - ∂p/∂s'' = 2Σx''x'' - 2Σx''x'', then (6) and (4)) gives linear part - 1/2 Σ (p_{ν,ιι'''} p_{ν',ι'ι''} - p_{ν,ιι''} p_{ν',ι'ι'''}) β_{νν'}/B = 0. A check on the unit sphere confirms the minus sign. Whether this is a slip by Riemann or by the transcriber needs checking against the image of folio 55v and the Werke.

results.what: Invariance of the quadrilinear curvature form II under change of coordinates (tensor character of the curvature)
results.modern_name: Riemann curvature tensor as a covariant 4-tensor
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1854 lecture; 1861 Commentatio, publ. 1876); Christoffel 1869 for the systematic invariant theory

results.what: Vanishing of II (R ≡ 0) is necessary for transformability to constant coefficients; sufficiency asserted on p.16
results.modern_name: Flatness criterion: a metric is locally Euclidean iff its Riemann tensor vanishes
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1854/1861; proofs by Christoffel and Lipschitz 1869-70

results.what: Formula (III): K = -1/2 II / (g(d,d)g(δ,δ)-g(d,δ)^2), invariant under coordinate change and under change of basis of the 2-plane
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Habilitationsvortrag 1854, explicit formula in the Commentatio 1861)

results.what: Extreme values of sectional curvature as invariants for the equivalence problem
results.modern_name: Curvature invariants / local equivalence of metrics (Christoffel's equivalence problem)

results.what: Geometric interpretation: surface of geodesics tangent to a 2-plane, whose Gaussian curvature equals (III)
